title: Check current ownership before mutating a reused resource name
applies_when: A leak hypothesis proposes unconditional cleanup after a filesystem root is rebound or a fork callback may replace a file descriptor; an asynchronous cache callback may outlive invalidation and a same-key replacement. Inspect current ownership and identity, not just the old pathname, fd number or cache key.
lesson: A pathname, fd number or cache key can designate a different resource by cleanup time. Async cache callbacks must compare the currently stored task/item identity before deletion or TTL scheduling, while still cancelling an old task when its own last waiter leaves. OpenClaw deliberately skips ordinary rollback and stage deletion after INSTALL_BASE_CHANGED; inspect the retained root identity and test an outside sentinel after a real root rebind. Filelock's complete before-fork callback first retries unverified descriptor identities; child cleanup closes only a matching device/inode. Persistent identity failure is a different case: an earlier child callback can reuse the fd for an unrelated file, so unconditional close can damage that replacement. Pair normal owned cleanup and recovered-identity closure with a real same-number fd replacement or root rebind. Seven selected upstream Linux fork cases passed, including registration/rollback failure and replacement-fd preservation. This refutes the truncated-callback explanation, not every possible leak.
avoid_when: Retained resources can still have operational costs, and identity checks alone do not eliminate races. Do not use this counterexample to waive prompt cleanup of known-owned failed acquisitions, late worker arrivals or successful ownership handoffs. Filelock evidence is seven selected Linux CPython fork cases with task-only generated version metadata, not full backend/platform or packaging qualification. OpenClaw evidence is source/test inspection only, not executed installation tests. Safe identity-bound cleanup may be possible; demonstrate its ownership contract rather than inferring authority from the old name or number. Async-lru has an existing proposed fix in PR797; this is not a new contribution. Its single-event-loop task identity check does not establish cross-thread or distributed generation safety, performance, maintainer acceptance or a full supported-Python matrix.

evidence.note: The stable-root check compares real paths; the ordinary temp cleanup recursively removes a pathname. Its existence does not authorize removal after replacement. Source inspection.
Ordinary mutation/removal is bound to the retained owner and root/directory identities. Source inspection.
The changed-root failure warns and skips the ordinary rollback/stage-deletion branch. Source inspection, not a generic missing-finally defect.
The rebound-root fixture requires an untouched outside target and a warning, unlike ordinary cleanup controls. These TypeScript tests were inspected, not run.
The before-fork callback invokes _verify_unverified_descriptors; child detachment skips unknown or nonmatching identities instead of closing by fd number alone.

Native Linux selected upstream tests passed: recovering fstat after registration/rollback failure permits child closure, while persistent identity failure plus an earlier child callback preserves a different file reusing the same fd. Failure injection covers these cases, not all lock behavior.

Existing unmerged replacement-race fix, found during bounded duplicate screening. Independently reproduced against current master 639c403: 12 event-controlled invalidation/clear/eviction x error/task cancellation/waiter cancellation/success cases fail before the same task-identity guards and pass afterward. Local candidate: Linux CPython3.12 full suite 101 pass/4 skip; Windows CPython3.12/3.14 direct regressions 12/12 each. These runs validate the local current-master repair, not an exact execution of PR797's older head. No competing PR was opened.

Old task callbacks may delete or start TTL only if the current same-key entry still belongs to their task. Last-waiter cancellation must still cancel its own detached task, while removing a cache entry only if that entry is the same cache item. Exercise successful completion as well as errors: a stale success can prematurely start a replacement's TTL without immediately deleting it. The same key alone is not ownership.
